text:
The Blues close a four-game road trip in Nashville after losing 5-4 in overtime at New Jersey on Wednesday, when Jesper Bratt won it for the Devils. They're 2-2-1 in their last five and playing without Dillon Dube. The Predators arrive on a three-game winning streak, the latest a 3-2 overtime win at Colorado in which Steven Stamkos got the winner and Vitali Pinchuk scored his first NHL goal. Nashville also won the first meeting this season, 5-2 on Oct. 17, and deserved it: 66% of simulated replays of the shots went its way.

Our numbers see an even game, with expected goals (the quality of chances) at 3.08 for NSH and 2.99 for STL. Both teams have been outchanced at five on five more often than not. Nashville's power play, at 0.74 expected goals per game, is the stronger of the two units, while STL sits at 0.55. In net, the projected starters are Joel Hofer and Juuse Saros, each about five goals saved above expected this season. Last year Hofer was at +11.1, while Saros was at -10.2, and Saros has been better lately: 3.8 over his last five starts.

For the Blues, Pius Suter is one goal from 100 career goals, and Mason McTavish, at 30%, is their likeliest scorer in our model. For Nashville, Stamkos (36% to score) and Filip Forsberg (33%) both scored in the last meeting's neighborhood: they have 9 and 8 points in five games against STL.
